title: Effective Classification of Quadratic Forms over Number Fields via Hasse–Witt Invariants

problemStatement.formal: \text{Two nondegenerate quadratic forms } Q_1, Q_2 \text{ over a number field } K \text{ are equivalent} \iff \dim Q_1 = \dim Q_2,\ \operatorname{disc} Q_1 = \operatorname{disc} Q_2,\ \text{and}\ \epsilon_v(Q_1) = \epsilon_v(Q_2)\ \forall\ v \text{ (Hasse–Minkowski). We seek an effective algorithm computing these invariants.}
problemStatement.plain: Hilbert's 11th problem asks for the theory of quadratic forms over number fields. Hasse–Minkowski reduces equivalence over K to equivalence over every completion K_v, leaving dimension, discriminant, and the Hasse–Witt invariant at each place as classifying data. We want an effective, formally specified algorithm that computes these invariants (via Hilbert symbols) and decides equivalence — over ℚ first, then general number fields.
whyMatters: It is the computational heart of Hilbert's 11th problem: the local–global principle is only useful with effective invariant computation.
Connects to Mathlib's growing quadratic-form and quadratic-reciprocity libraries.

knownResults.goal: Formalize over ℚ the Hasse–Witt invariant via Hilbert symbols, the product formula, and the equivalence decision procedure; state the number-field generalization with local-field inputs as hypotheses.
